title: Mallakhamb OCI resources
description: The VMs themselves (OCI A1, 1 OCPU / 6 GB per VM, plus db-03, the Always Free micro VM that is the replica set's third member): CPU, memory, disk, network, the Always Free allowance, idle-reclaim risk, what OCI is charging, and what runs on them. Alloy, scrape_job mallakhamb-host (active) / mallakhamb-host-standby / mallakhamb-db.

list.name: cpu_limit
list.label: CPU limit, cores (one Node event loop; OCI A1, 1 OCPU / 6 GB per VM)

list.name: mem_limit
list.label: Memory budget for the API process, bytes (3 GiB; OCI A1, 1 OCPU / 6 GB per VM)

list.name: sm_included
list.label: Synthetic check executions included per month (free tier)

list.name: free_mem
list.label: Always Free A1 memory, bytes (whole tenancy)

list.name: free_block
list.label: Always Free block + boot volume storage, bytes

list.name: free_egress
list.label: Always Free outbound data per month, bytes

list.name: nic_bps
list.label: Network bandwidth of a 1-OCPU A1 VM, bits/s

panels.title: VMs
panels.description: Role and release on each VM. Both should show the same sha (alert "Standby behind the active").

panels.title: Reporting
panels.description: UP = Alloy sent a sample in the last 5 minutes. DOWN = it reported in the last day but has gone quiet: the VM is stopped, or Alloy is (systemctl status alloy).

panels.title: Uptime
panels.description: Since the last kernel boot.

panels.title: OCPUs
panels.description: Cores the kernel sees. On A1, 1 OCPU = 1 core.

panels.title: CPU busy %
panels.description: All cores, every process, last 5 minutes. Bands at 70 / 80 / 90 %.

panels.title: Memory used %
panels.description: 1 − MemAvailable / MemTotal. Alert "Host memory high" at 85 % on the active.

panels.title: Root disk used %
panels.description: Alerts "Disk filling" at 80 % and 90 %.

panels.title: Always Free allowance: the whole tenancy, every VM counted (deploy/oci/PLAN.md)
A1 OCPUs % of free (2)
panels.description: Cores of the two A1 VMs against the 2 A1 OCPUs Always Free allows since 2026-06-15. Two 1-OCPU VMs = 100 %: that is the whole allowance, by design, so it stays green up to 100 %. The root quota mallakhamb-prod-quota-free-tier stops a launch past it.

panels.title: A1 memory % of free (12 GB)
panels.description: MemTotal of the two A1 VMs against the 12 GB Always Free allows. Two 4 GB VMs since 2026-10-24 (IDLE-RECLAIM-PLAN.md D1) read about 64 %; the kernel keeps some memory for itself. Green up to 100 %; never resize past it.

panels.title: AMD micro VMs % of free (2)
panels.description: db-03 (VM.Standard.E2.1.Micro) against the 2 Always Free micro VMs. The root quota allows exactly 1 (standard-e2-micro-core-count = 1), so 50 % is the most this can read.

panels.title: Boot volumes % of free (200 GB)
panels.description: Root filesystem size of every VM (three 50 GB boot volumes) against the 200 GB of block storage Always Free allows. Volume backups are a separate allowance (5).

panels.title: Outbound data % of free (10 TB / month)
panels.description: Bytes sent by every VM over the last 7 days, projected to 30 days, against the 10 TB a month Always Free includes.

panels.title: Idle reclaim: Oracle may reclaim an Always Free VM that is idle for 7 days
CPU p95 (7d)
panels.description: 95th percentile of CPU busy % over 7 days. Oracle's rule: a VM is idle when CPU p95, network and memory are ALL below 20 % for 7 days. Red = below 20 %.

panels.title: Memory p95 (7d)
panels.description: Memory used % over 7 days (95th percentile). The memory test applies to A1 shapes. Red = below 20 %.

panels.title: Network p95 (7d)

targets.expr: quantile_over_time(0.95, (100 * 8 * (sum by (instance) (max by (instance, device) (rate(node_network_receive_bytes_total{scrape_job=~"mallakhamb-host|mallakhamb-host-standby|mallakhamb-db",instance=~"$instance",device!="lo"}[5m]))) + sum by (instance) (max by (instance, device) (rate(node_network_transmit_bytes_total{scrape_job=~"mallakhamb-host|mallakhamb-host-standby|mallakhamb-db",instance=~"$instance",device!="lo"}[5m])))) / $nic_bps)[7d:5m])

panels.description: In + out as a share of the 1 Gbps a 1-OCPU A1 VM gets. Always red here: this app never comes near 20 % of a gigabit.

options.content:
Reclaim needs **all three** below 20 % for 7 days, measured by Oracle on its own agent; these numbers are the same tests from Alloy, so treat them as close, not exact.

Light traffic leaves **both** VMs red here, not just the standby. CPU or memory steadily above 20 % on a VM takes it out of the rule.

panels.title: CPU busy %
panels.description: All cores, every process. Dashed lines: 70 / 80 / 90 %.

panels.title: CPU steal %
panels.description: Time the hypervisor gave this core to another tenant. Steady steal above a few % makes everything slower without the VM looking busy.

panels.title: CPU by mode: $instance
panels.description: user = the API, OCR and scripts; system = the kernel; iowait = waiting on the boot volume; steal = the hypervisor.

panels.title: Load vs cores
panels.description: Runnable + waiting tasks. Load above the core count for long = the VM is the bottleneck.

panels.title: Pressure stall (PSI)
panels.description: Share of time at least one task was waiting for CPU, memory or disk. The earliest sign of a VM that is too small.

panels.title: Memory: $instance

targets.expr: max by (instance) (node_memory_MemTotal_bytes{scrape_job=~"mallakhamb-host|mallakhamb-host-standby|mallakhamb-db",instance=~"$instance"}) - max by (instance) (node_memory_MemFree_bytes{scrape_job=~"mallakhamb-host|mallakhamb-host-standby|mallakhamb-db",instance=~"$instance"}) - max by (instance) (node_memory_Buffers_bytes{scrape_job=~"mallakhamb-host|mallakhamb-host-standby|mallakhamb-db",instance=~"$instance"}) - max by (instance) (node_memory_Cached_bytes{scrape_job=~"mallakhamb-host|mallakhamb-host-standby|mallakhamb-db",instance=~"$instance"}) - max by (instance) (node_memory_SReclaimable_bytes{scrape_job=~"mallakhamb-host|mallakhamb-host-standby|mallakhamb-db",instance=~"$instance"})

max by (instance) (node_memory_Buffers_bytes{scrape_job=~"mallakhamb-host|mallakhamb-host-standby|mallakhamb-db",instance=~"$instance"}) + max by (instance) (node_memory_Cached_bytes{scrape_job=~"mallakhamb-host|mallakhamb-host-standby|mallakhamb-db",instance=~"$instance"}) + max by (instance) (node_memory_SReclaimable_bytes{scrape_job=~"mallakhamb-host|mallakhamb-host-standby|mallakhamb-db",instance=~"$instance"})

panels.description: Stacks to the VM total. The cache is given back on demand, so only "used by processes" is pressure.

panels.title: Swap used
panels.description: Flat zero when the VM has no swap file.

panels.title: Major page faults/s
panels.description: Pages read back from disk. A rise together with high memory = the VM is thrashing.

panels.title: OOM kills (1h)
panels.description: The kernel killed a process for memory. Alert "Out-of-memory kill" pages on any.

panels.title: Filesystem used %

targets.expr: 100 * (1 - max by (instance, mountpoint) (node_filesystem_avail_bytes{scrape_job=~"mallakhamb-host|mallakhamb-host-standby|mallakhamb-db",instance=~"$instance",fstype!~"tmpfs|ramfs|squashfs|overlay"}) / max by (instance, mountpoint) (node_filesystem_size_bytes{scrape_job=~"mallakhamb-host|mallakhamb-host-standby|mallakhamb-db",instance=~"$instance",fstype!~"tmpfs|ramfs|squashfs|overlay"}))

panels.description: Every real mount. Dashed lines: 70 / 80 / 90 %.

panels.title: Root disk free
panels.description: Backups are written locally before the upload to Object Storage, so a dip each night is normal.

panels.title: Disk throughput
panels.description: Boot volume. Its limits scale with size (Balanced: 60 IOPS and 480 KB/s per GB).

panels.title: Disk busy %
panels.description: Share of time the volume had a request in flight. Near 100 % with iowait in the CPU panel = the disk is the bottleneck.

panels.title: Throughput
panels.description: Every interface except loopback.

panels.title: Errors and drops
panels.description: Should be flat zero.

panels.title: Data sent per day
panels.description: Rolling 24-hour total of outbound bytes. Competition days and nightly backups show as humps.

panels.title: API (active VM)
panels.description: Grafana Cloud scraped the API on the reserved IP. The standby runs no API.

panels.title: API memory vs the VM
panels.description: How much of the active VM the API takes. The rest is Caddy, the OCR reader, Alloy and the page cache.

panels.title: OCR reader
panels.description: Walk-in desk sidecar, active VM only (deploy/oci/PLAN.md O15).

panels.title: Last backup age
panels.description: The nightly backup runs on the active; alert "Backup stale" above 26 h. A standby keeps the age it was cloned with.

panels.title: Nightly e2e: last pass
panels.description: Time since the nightly lifecycle run (deploy/oci/PLAN.md O14) last passed on each VM.

panels.title: Nightly e2e: last result
panels.description: FAIL → journalctl -u mallakhamb-e2e on that VM.

panels.title: OCI cost: budget mallakhamb-guard (SGD, the tenancy currency; Always Free = 0)
Charged this month
panels.description: What OCI has charged so far this month. Anything above 0 means something paid exists: alert "OCI is charging money" (critical, emails the owner); OCI's own budget alert emails too.

panels.title: Forecast for the month
panels.description: OCI's forecast for the whole month. Alert "OCI forecast over the budget" above the SGD 1.50 guard.

panels.title: Forecast % of the guard
panels.description: Forecast spend against the budget (SGD 1.50, about Rs 100). Bands at 70 / 80 / 90 %.

panels.title: Cost data age
panels.description: Since the budget was last read (hourly). Alert "OCI cost data stale" above 3 h, because then the cost alerts are blind. OCI updates the spend a few times a day.

panels.title: Oracle's idle test: its own agent metrics, 7-day p95 (an Always Free VM may be stopped when every measure is under 20 %)
May Oracle stop it?
panels.description: Oracle rule: CPU p95, network and (A1 only) memory all under 20 % for 7 days. Red is not an outage: Oracle emails mallakhambindia@gmail.com a week before it stops anything, and the Resource Scheduler starts a stopped VM within 30 min. Runbook: deploy/oci/IDLE-RECLAIM-PLAN.md.

panels.title: Memory p95 (counts for A1)
panels.description: OCI MemoryUtilization, 7-day p95. Counts only for the A1 VMs (app-01, app-02; 4 GB since 2026-10-24); not for db-03.

panels.title: CPU p95
panels.description: OCI CpuUtilization, 7-day p95 of 5-minute means.

panels.title: Oracle data age
panels.description: Since mallakhamb-oci-idle last read OCI Monitoring (hourly at :41). Stale: journalctl -u mallakhamb-oci-idle; policy mallakhamb-prod-pol-metrics-read.
